Expectation1: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation1: Your friend calls you in the middle of the night, crying, because they just received some devastating family news.
Expectation2: Organize and participate in peaceful protests to raise awareness about social issues.
Situation2: Police have just begun to unexpectedly block the exits of the protest area, and you must immediately help coordinate a safe response.
Story: My phone buzzed violently on the cold pavement, the protest’s energy still pulsing in my veins. I glanced at the screen—Maya. I answered, her voice trembling, words tumbling out about her father’s sudden heart attack. She was sobbing, lost, needing me to listen, to be her anchor. I pressed the phone to my ear, heart aching for her, but all around me, shouts rose as police began blocking the exits. My fellow activists looked to me, expecting calm leadership, quick thinking, a plan to keep everyone safe. I could hear Maya’s pain, but I could also see the fear in my friends’ eyes. I wanted to be there for her, to listen, to comfort, but I was also needed here, right now, to help dozens of people avoid panic and danger. My mind raced, torn between the desperate voice in my ear and the urgent chaos around me, feeling the weight of both worlds pressing in, demanding everything at once.
